scope: Historical audit 1700-1945 of Southern Asia (Natural Earth subregion: Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Iran, Maldives, Nepal, Pakistan, Sri Lanka). Compared Cliopatria v0.2.0 coverage maps for sample years 1700-1945 with Wikipedia, Wikidata (every QID verified with the API), the Imperial Gazetteer of India and other cited works; fixes mislabelled and ghost territories, adds missing states, colonial enclaves, princely states and indigenous peoples where sources describe extents, and lists known gaps.

entries.reason: Cliopatria labels the Qajar state with its dynasty ('Qajar Dynasty', Wikidata Q189326 = the dynasty item). The polity on the map is the state, called Persia in English at the time (officially the 'Sublime State of Persia' / Guarded Domains of Iran, 1789-1925). Display name set to the period English name 'Persia', with the dynastic and official names as altNames; Wikidata switched to the state item Q63158027 'Qajar Iran (country 1789-1925)', verified with the Wikidata API.
entries.author: agent:audit-h-southern-asia

entries.reason: Cliopatria swaps two labels in 1895-1897: the record covering Iran is named 'Dutch East Indies' and the record covering the Dutch East Indies is named 'Qajar Dynasty'. Iran was Qajar Persia throughout (Naser al-Din Shah to 1896, then Mozaffar ad-Din Shah). Re-adds Persia with its own 1894 geometry; the tier-0 add carves Iran out of the mislabelled 'Dutch East Indies' record. Companion entry h-southern-asia-0003 fixes the Indonesian side.

entries.reason: Companion of h-southern-asia-0002: in 1895-1897 Cliopatria's record over the Dutch East Indies (Indonesia, 61 parts) is labelled 'Qajar Dynasty' while the 'Dutch East Indies' record covers Iran. Re-adds the Dutch East Indies with Cliopatria's own 1898 Dutch East Indies geometry (the same shape, area within 1%), which carves the Indonesian area out of the mislabelled 'Qajar' record. Reviewer note: the south-eastern-asia file may fix the same swap from the other side - keep only one of the two re-adds.

entries.reason: During the First World War Persia was a neutral, sovereign state whose territory was fought over and partly occupied by Russian, British and Ottoman forces (Persian campaign). Cliopatria carves Iran into 'Russian Empire' (north, 1915-1916), 'British Colonial Empire' (Bushehr coast 1915-1917, then the Norperforce road and the south-west 1918-1921), 'British Africa' (1919) and 'Ottoman Empire' (1915) as if annexed. Per the editorial policy occupied areas are not tier-0 territory: Persia is restored with its 1914 extent; the occupations are recorded in the known-gap entry h-southern-asia-0005.
entries.author: agent:audit-h-southern-asia

entries.reason: Known gap (not drawn): foreign military occupation of neutral Persia, to be added as tier-1 'disputed' overlays when sourced extents are collected - Russian troops in the north (Tabriz, Rasht, Qazvin, Mashhad) from 1909/1911 until their withdrawal in 1917-1918; Ottoman operations in Azerbaijan and Kermanshah-Hamadan 1914-1918; British forces at Bushehr (1915-1916), the East Persia Cordon (Seistan Force) in Sistan (1915-1920), the South Persia Rifles in Fars and Kerman (1916-1921) and Norperforce on the Baghdad-Kermanshah-Hamadan-Qazvin-Enzeli road (1918-1921). Cliopatria's shapes for these (see h-southern-asia-0004) are a usable starting point but were not verified.
entries.author: agent:audit-h-southern-asia

entries.reason: Cliopatria starts the Pahlavi state in 1924. The Qajar dynasty was deposed by the Majles on 31 October 1925 and Reza Khan was proclaimed Shah on 12-15 December 1925, so Persia was still Qajar at the end of 1924. Re-adds Qajar Persia for 1924 with its 1923 geometry (carving the early 'Pahlavi Dynasty' record); the Pahlavi state starts in 1925.
entries.author: agent:audit-h-southern-asia

entries.reason: The Pahlavi state (from December 1925) was known in English as Persia (the 'Imperial State of Persia') until Reza Shah asked foreign governments to use 'Iran' in 1935. Display name set to the period name; Wikidata switched from the dynasty item Q207991 to the state item Q107258515 'Pahlavi Iran (former sovereign state 1925-1979)', verified with the Wikidata API. (1924 is re-assigned to the Qajars by h-southern-asia-0006.)

entries.reason: From 21 March 1935 the country asked to be called Iran internationally ('Imperial State of Iran'). Display name 'Iran'; Wikidata set to the state item Q107258515 'Pahlavi Iran' (verified).

entries.reason: Cliopatria cuts Iran into 'British Colonial Empire', 'British Africa' and 'Union of Soviet Socialist Republics' records in 1942-1945. Iran remained a sovereign state under Anglo-Soviet military occupation (invasion of 25 August 1941; Tripartite Treaty of January 1942; withdrawal March-May 1946). Restores Iran with its 1941 extent in tier 0; the two occupation zones become tier-1 overlays (h-southern-asia-0010, -0011).
entries.author: agent:audit-h-southern-asia

entries.reason: Soviet occupation of northern Iran from the invasion of 25-31 August 1941 (Soviet and British forces met at Sanandaj and Qazvin) until the Soviet withdrawal in May 1946. Tier-1 overlay over sovereign Iran; extent = Cliopatria's 1943 Soviet record intersected with Iran (Azerbaijan, Gilan, Mazandaran, Gorgan and northern Khorasan), approximate.
entries.author: agent:audit-h-southern-asia

entries.reason: British (Paiforce) occupation of south-western Iran - Khuzestan oilfields and Abadan, Kermanshah, Hamadan and the road to Qazvin - from August 1941 until the British withdrawal of March 1946 (the US Persian Gulf Command ran the southern railway from 1942). Tier-1 overlay; extent = Cliopatria's 1943 'British Colonial Empire' record intersected with Iran, approximate.

entries.reason: Cliopatria gives the whole Iranian plateau to the Hotaki (Afghan) dynasty until 1733. Nader Khan defeated Ashraf Hotak at Damghan and Murche-Khort in late 1729 and restored the Safavid Tahmasp II at Isfahan; the Hotakis kept only Kandahar until 1738, and the Safavid line (Tahmasp II, then the infant Abbas III from 1732) reigned until Nader's coronation in 1736. Adds the Safavid state over the Iranian part of Cliopatria's 1730 Hotaki record (Cliopatria's Safavid name and Wikidata kept for continuity with its pre-1700 records).
entries.author: agent:audit-h-southern-asia

entries.reason: Cliopatria starts 'Afsharid Iran' in 1734, but Nader ruled as regent for the Safavid Abbas III until he was crowned Shah on 8 March 1736 (Mughan assembly), which is the conventional start of Afsharid Iran (Wikidata Q63149558: 1736-1796). Re-labels 1734-1735 as Safavid using Cliopatria's 1735 Afsharid geometry.
entries.author: agent:audit-h-southern-asia

entries.reason: Known gap: 1722-1729 Iran is drawn wrongly by Cliopatria (Safavid over most of Iran until 1726, then Hotaki over everything 1727-1733). After the fall of Isfahan (October 1722) the Hotakis (Mahmud, then Ashraf) held Isfahan, Kashan, Qom, Kerman and Fars; Tahmasp II kept Mazandaran and Astarabad (and Khorasan after Nader took Mashhad in 1726); the Ottomans occupied the west (Hamadan, Kermanshah, Tabriz, 1723-1730s) and Russia the Caspian provinces (1722-1732/35). Needs sourced period maps before it can be drawn.
entries.author: agent:audit-h-southern-asia

entries.reason: Missing polity: the Persian Socialist Soviet Republic (Gilan Republic), proclaimed at Rasht in May-June 1920 by the Jangali movement with Soviet support and ended in September 1921 (Russo-Persian treaty of February 1921, Soviet withdrawal, reconquest by Reza Khan's forces). De facto state controlling Gilan at the end of 1920; drawn as Gilan province (approximate - its hold on neighbouring Mazandaran was brief).

entries.reason: Editorial decision: Iran's tribal confederacies (Bakhtiari, Qashqai, Lurs, Kurdish emirates such as Ardalan, Baluch chiefdoms, Turkmen Yomut and Goklen) and the autonomous Arab sheikhdom of Mohammerah in Khuzestan (Bani Ka'b / Sheikh Khaz'al, to 1924-1925) are not drawn. They were autonomous within the Persian state and sources give no stable territorial extents for 1700-1945; candidates for future tier-1 overlays.

entries.reason: Cliopatria has no Kingdom of Kandy: its interior polygon of Sri Lanka is labelled 'Dutch Ceylon' (1687-1768) while the real Dutch coastal possessions are labelled 'Dutch Republic'. Kandy stayed independent of the Dutch (who never controlled it) and still reached the sea on the east coast and at Puttalam/Chilaw until the war of 1761-1765. Re-labels Cliopatria's interior polygon as Kandy.

sources.title: Codrington, A Short History of Lanka (1926), ch. 9 (Dutch period): treaty of 14 February 1766

entries.reason: Kingdom of Kandy after the treaty of 14 February 1766, by which the king ceded to the Dutch East India Company all districts bordering the coast, leaving Kandy landlocked; it stayed so under the British (from 1796) until the Kandyan Convention of 2 March 1815. Uses Cliopatria's post-treaty interior polygon (labelled 'Dutch Ceylon' 1769-1795 and 'British Ceylon' 1796-1814 in Cliopatria; Cliopatria also dates the change to 1769 instead of 1766).

sources.title: Codrington, A Short History of Lanka (1926), ch. 9 (Dutch period): treaty of 14 February 1766

Drawn as Sri Lanka minus Kandy (h-southern-asia-0701). The pid is re-used because Cliopatria's own 'Dutch Ceylon' record is the interior (Kandy) and is carved away by h-southern-asia-0701 (expect a validator warning about a re-added Cliopatria pid).

entries.reason: British Ceylon 1796-1814 = the former Dutch maritime provinces (Crown colony from 1 January 1802, confirmed by the Treaty of Amiens). Cliopatria labels this belt 'British Empire' and puts the name 'British Ceylon' on the independent Kandyan interior. Drawn as Sri Lanka minus Kandy; the pid is re-used (validator warning expected) because Cliopatria's own record is carved away by h-southern-asia-0702.

entries.reason: After the Kandyan Convention (2 March 1815) the whole island was the Crown colony of British Ceylon until independence (1948). Cliopatria folds Ceylon into 'British Empire' (1815-1858) and 'British Raj' (1859-1945), but Ceylon was never part of British India: it was a separate Crown colony under the Colonial Office. Tier-0 add of the whole island carves it out of those records.

entries.reason: Missing: the Lakshadweep islands (uncovered in Cliopatria and too far offshore for automatic island assignment) were held as a jagir by the Muslim Arakkal dynasty (Ali Rajas / Bibis of Cannanore) from the mid-16th century. Drawn as all Natural Earth Lakshadweep islands (the dynasty's small mainland seat at Cannanore is below the map's granularity).

entries.reason: The northern Amindivi group (Amini, Kadmat, Kiltan, Chetlat, Bitra) revolted against Cannanore and came under Tipu Sultan's Mysore in 1787; the rest of the islands stayed with the Arakkal Bibi. Arakkal keeps the southern (Laccadive and Minicoy) islands here; the Amindivi go to Mysore (h-southern-asia-0722).

entries.reason: Indigenous peoples missing from Cliopatria: the Great Andaman islands were the territory of the Great Andamanese (some ten tribes, among them the Aka-Bea, Aka-Jeru, Aka-Bo) and of the Jarawa (south-west of South and Middle Andaman). Tier-1 overlay over whatever holds the islands (nothing until the short British settlement of 1789-1796 and the Port Blair penal colony from 1858). The Great Andamanese were devastated by epidemics after 1858; the overlay records their homeland, not population.
